scenarios.description:
Smoothness scenario meant to test your ability to stay precise and controlled during arcing motions and bounces.
Focus on having your arm and hand relaxed.

scenarios.name: PureG Fuglaa React
scenarios.description:
This features three bots in a gauntlet style with unique strafe patterns. 
This will test you on your reactivity, smoothness, and reading skills. 
Try to smoothly react to bot changes in movement instead of frantic flicks, and generally prioritize keeping your crosshair in the middle of the bot to maximize your score. 
After acquiring the target try to match the bot's velocity.

scenarios.name: PureG Glider
scenarios.description:
This scenario is meant to constructively test you on smooth tracking while minimizing your ability to game the scenario. 
Track a precise, non-reactive bot over long distances on both vertical and horizontal angles. 
Try to keep as little tension in your hand and arm as possible.

scenarios.name: PureG Horizontal Clicking
scenarios.description:
This scenario will test you on your flick accuracy, speed and tempo on moving targets. 
Focus on maintaining good tempo and try to avoid waiting for targets to enter your crosshair. 
Prioritize underflicking.

scenarios.name: PureG KinTS
scenarios.description:
A classic scenario meant to test your target switching against evasively moving targets with higher time to kill (TTK) on wide angles. 
Play in 110-125 Overwatch FOV, and hold down mouse1 for the duration of the scenario. 
Focus on your stability, clean lines, target selection, and flick accuracy before prioritizing speed.

scenarios.name: PureG Leapcorn
scenarios.description:
This scenario features fast moving 1-hit kill bots moving in a low arc pattern. 
You get 6 shots before reloading is required. 
This primarily tests you on your reading, timing, and stability after flicking to each target. 
Prioritize shooting bots immediately after the peak of their arc.

scenarios.name: PureG Pasu Switch
scenarios.description:
This scenario is meant to test your target switching against evasively moving targets with higher time to kill (TTK). 
Hold down mouse1 for the duration of the scenario. focus on your stability, clean lines, target selection, and flick accuracy before prioritizing speed.

scenarios.name: PureG Pill Switch
scenarios.description:
This scenario primarily tests you on your speed to switch between targets, but requires flick accuracy, stability and target selection strategy to get high scores. 
Try to immediately flick to the next target right as your current target is eliminated. 
Play in 115-125 Overwatch FOV if desired, and hold down m1 for the duration of the scenario.

scenarios.name: PureG Pokeball
scenarios.description:
This scenario tests you on your static technique requiring precise, accurate flicks and kill confirmation over raw speed. 
Each bot has a small amount of health that regenerates so you have to ensure each target is completely dead before moving on. Hold down m1 for the duration of the scenario and prioritize underflicking.

scenarios.name: PureG Static Clicking
scenarios.description:
This scenario tests you both on small precise and accurate clicking and your flick speed. 
It features bots that are very small in size at the beginning and as you eliminate them, they become progressively larger in size to emphasize the speed component. prioritize underflicking and if you miss a target, do not go back and confirm it. simply move on to maintain tempo.

scenarios.name: PureG Static Switching
scenarios.description:
This tests you mostly on your raw switching speed across random angles and distances. 
Run at 115-125 Overwatch FOV and hold down m1 for the duration of the scenario. 
Prioritize clusters of bots and minimize distance traveled across your field of view.

scenarios.name: PureG Thin Strafes
scenarios.description: This is a horizontal tracking thin bot with somewhat reactive changes in direction in order to challenge your smoothness, reading, and reactivity skills. [n1]Focus on keeping as little tension in your hand, smoothly reacting to target changes in movement, and avoiding prediction by assuming the target will keep going in it's current direction forever. [n1]Treat the changes in direction as decelerating then re-accelerating instead of snappy flicks.

scenarios.name: VT AirStrafe Advanced
scenarios.description:
A single invincible bot makes fast and sporadic X/Y/Z strafes while the player navigates the space as they shoot. 

In this scenario, MBS scoring is used - by default you should see a bar that fills up as you move. As long as you change direction while the bar is green, you get maximum movement score. The bar is almost always green. If you keep moving while the bar is full, you don't get any score. The score is capped to a value that is easy to reach as long as you move throughout the scenario. You should find ways to move in ways that makes aiming easy.

scenarios.name: VT PatStrafe Advanced
scenarios.description:
A single bot makes fast and sporadic strafes on a flat surface and continuously respawns after it's eliminated, all while the player navigates the space as they shoot. 

In this scenario, conditional distance travelled scoring is used and is capped to 1000. As long as you don't mirror every bot 100% of the time, you will reach the score cap. If you only mirror during the run, you will not reach the movement score cap. If you only anti-mirror you will easily reach score cap but your accuracy will suffer. You should mix up your movement and focus on accuracy.
